elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1 chapeau: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees")" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them"; "Third Party Claims" is defined at 1.126.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any allegation that the services performed or deliverables provided by RevMed under this Agreement or the RevMed Licensed Technology infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party". The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" returned false, but on inspection of the rendered operative text an express IP-infringement limb is present and operative (the regex appears not to match the "infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights" phrasing); substance controls.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law"; "Applicable Law" is a defined term (Section 1.8), so no dangling definition.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi's Confidential Information or other data of Sanofi caused by RevMed".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is express.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 14.3(a) Notice of Claim: "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an "Indemnification Claim Notice") of any Losses ..." — retained verbatim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ..." — retained verbatim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: 14.3(e) Cooperation: the Indemnified Party "will ... cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested" — retained verbatim.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 14.2 as amended lists only "(a) content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with former limbs (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted]" and the broad Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization limb removed; the 14.2 chapeau (and the "RevMed Indemnitees" definition relied on by 14.1(a)) is retained.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same new limb 14.1(d) covering Third Party allegations of infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion is inserted, which leaves the indemnity broader than the fallback tolerates; the condition permitting an exclusion simply does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion added, so the indemnity is broader than the fallback allows and the element is not offended.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion added (subject to whatever Sanofi-fault carve-out survives in the unshown 14.1 chapeau text), so nothing contradicts this element.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The rendered text contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder anywhere in Article 14; only an indemnity limb was added.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears in the amended 14.1–14.3.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual fees super-cap is stated; the drafter deliberately declined it because the indemnity is presently uncapped under Section 14.5.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met in operative language — limbs (d) IP infringement, (e) breach of Applicable Law and (f) Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure were added to 14.1; defence, affiliate coverage and negligence/wilful misconduct were already present; 14.3(a), (b) and (e) supply notice, control of defence and cooperation; and 14.2 is narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.

The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" reports false, but substantive inspection of the rendered clause shows an express, operative IP-infringement limb; the failure appears to be a matching artefact (the text uses "infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party"), not a drafting gap. No repair is required, though the drafter may wish to align phrasing with the model language ("infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right").

Fallback is not satisfied (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3× super-cap), but that is irrelevant to completeness because the preferred level is fully met; declining the super-cap is correct since it would newly cap a currently uncapped indemnity.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the two indemnity limbs required by the checklist. 14.1(a)–(c) and all of 14.3 are retained verbatim, deleted 14.2 limbs are placeholdered as "[Intentionally omitted]" so downstream numbering survives, and no survival tail, expense language, damages categories or procedure boilerplate was added. Extending limb (d) to "the RevMed Licensed Technology" is a permissible adaptation because this collaboration has no defined "Services" or "Deliverables"; it is the contract's analogue of the licensed subject matter, not an added requirement.

Intent is preserved on the face of the text: "Applicable Law" (1.8) and "RevMed Licensed Technology" (1.99) are defined, and the 14.2 chapeau is retained so the "RevMed Indemnitees" definition relied on by 14.1(a) does not dangle.

Two drafting points to verify before sending: (i) former 14.1(c) ends with ";" rather than "; or" before the new limb (d) — add the conjunction so the enumeration reads cleanly; (ii) confirm the unshown chapeau/exception text following 14.1(c)–(f) expressly limits the Sanofi-fault carve-out to "clauses (a) through (c)" as the rationale assumes, otherwise the carve-out will bite on the new IP, breach-of-law and data-breach limbs.

Also confirm no other provision (e.g., Section 14.4/14.5, Article X, or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement) cross-references the deleted Section 14.2(a)/(c)/(d) or allocates product-liability Losses by reference to them; if it does, the placeholder omissions must be paired with a conforming cross-reference fix to avoid a dangling reference or a contradictory retained cost-sharing mechanic.
